items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy Thanksgiving geography fun-fact Short for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel. The Narrator is SUPER excited, practically bursting with energy: a hyped-up, thrilled YouTube host who can't believe how funny this mix-up is and can't wait to tell you. Huge smile in the voice the whole way, bright and punchy, loud-ish and lively. Wide, dramatic pitch movement: rise with real wonder on every question, hit every number with genuine amazement, and land each punchline with a grin after a tiny comic pause. The country-by-country names (France, Portugal, Arabic, Malaysia) are a rapid, giggly list, each one funnier than the last. 'And it gets even weirder' is whispered-excited, leaning in like a secret. Mexico's line is a cheeky, slightly offended little voice-wink. The last line trails off unfinished, voice staying up, so it loops straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 175 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy, bored or documentary-serious. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same high energy level throughout. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. Pronounce Türkiye as tur-kee-YAY, guajolote as gwah-ho-LOH-teh, dinde as DAND (French), peru as peh-ROO, Aztecs as AZ-teks, guinea fowl as GIH-nee fowl. The word Hindi (the Turkish name for the bird) is said like the language name, HIN-dee, with a big surprised emphasis. turki is said TUR-kee.
lines: A bird named after a country it's not even from.
It's actually from Mexico. The Aztecs raised turkeys over two thousand years ago.
In the fifteen hundreds, the Spanish shipped them to Europe.
But Europe got confused. It looked like the guinea fowl... an African bird that came through Turkish lands.
So the English just called it... turkey.
But what does Turkey call it?
And in India? In Hindi, it's called... turki!
Every country named it after somewhere else.
In twenty twenty-two, Turkey asked the UN to say Türkiye... partly to ditch the bird.
And Mexico? Guys... it's mine. We call it guajolote!
